paper_title: Open Problem: Tight Characterization of Instance-Optimal Identity Testing
statement: Open Question 1 Is there a “succinct” functional Φ : ∆(X )×(0, 1] → N which fully characterizes the sample complexity of massively parameterized identity testing, (or, say, up to constant factors)? If so, what is it? If not, can we prove such a quantity cannot exist? (Note that the “succinctness” requirement here is a little vague. Ideally, Φ should either have a closed form, or be efficiently computable given the explicit description of the reference distribution q.)
